headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill directs Dominion Energy Virginia to propose rates that shift the costs of increasing electric generating capacity and distribution infrastructure to large energy users, specifically those with 25 MW or greater demand, aiming to protect residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, Governor's administration, consumer advocacy groups, some state lawmakers.
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users (though some exceptions exist for manufacturing).
news_headline: Virginia orders data centers to pay for new transmission infrastructure
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission ordered data centers to cover transmission infrastructure costs exclusively tied to their facilities, a move supported by the governor's administration to prevent these expenses from being spread across other ratepayers. This decision is projected to save Virginians hundreds of millions of dollars by assigning costs to the large customers responsible for creating the need for the infrastructure.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates waterworks operators to categorize and report monthly water sales data, including usage by data centers, to increase transparency regarding water consumption.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, transparency advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (due to reporting burden, though some acknowledge the need for transparency).
news_headline: New regulations beef up data centers' required water use reporting in Virginia
news_summary: New regulations, effective January 2027, will require waterworks operators to categorize monthly water sales data, including usage by data centers, to provide more transparency on water consumption in Virginia. This legislation, carried by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, aims to fill a data gap for water supply planning, especially during droughts.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for sound profiles near residential areas and schools, and allowing localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data centers, environmental groups, Delegate Joshua Thomas.
opponents: Data center industry, developers (due to increased regulatory burden and potential siting restrictions).
news_headline: Subcommittee advances revised data-center siting bill after mixed testimony
news_summary: House Bill 153, a revised package of siting and disclosure rules for data centers, passed a subcommittee after negotiations between supporters and industry groups. The bill mandates sound studies near residential areas and allows localities to require assessments of environmental impacts.
